title: Double-gate in wolfssl_ec_key helpers is correct defense-in-depth
description: wolfssl_ec_key_export_public() and wolfssl_ec_key_export_private() call wolfssl_fips_gate() directly at their entry point, even though the per-algo wrappers in wolfssl_ecdsa.c and wolfssl_ecdh.c also call it before delegating. The comment in wolfssl_ec_key.c is explicit: 'The helpers are called from gated per-algo wrappers today, but the gate lives here so no future caller can bypass it by accident.' The file header also documents: 'Per-algo wrappers in each .c file call wolfssl_fips_gate() before delegating to these functions.' The double-gate is the correct defense-in-depth posture: shared helper functions that perform cryptographic operations must not rely on their callers having already checked FIPS status. If a new call site is added — another file, a refactor, a test harness — that omits the gate at the wrapper layer, the helper's own gate prevents any bypass. A reviewer might suggest removing the 'redundant' gate from the helper to simplify call paths. That removal would leave these helpers unguarded if ever called directly, which is a FIPS compliance failure that the compiler cannot catch.
close_reason: Design decision confirmed by code inspection — no code change required.
